description.narrative:
Bangladesh, Nepal. SUF works primarily with providing income-generating knowledge and skills to young people, both through non-formal education for working children and through vocational training for youth and economically marginalised individuals. They describe their target demographic as the ‘poorest of the poor’ in both the urban and rural areas of Dhaka city and district. Although not specifically stated in the FS application, SUF’s work correlates with SDG # 1, ‘No poverty’, SDG #4 ‘Quality education’, and SDG #8 ‘Decent work and economic growth’.
EWN works to empower, educate and create employment opportunities to improve the lives of disadvantaged Nepali women and girls through training in adventure tourism, entrepreneurial skills development and educational scholarships. Their target group is socio-economically disadvantaged young females, and their work is in line with SDG # 4 ‘Quality education’, SDG #5 ‘Gender equality’, SDG # 8, ‘Decent work and economic growth, and SDG # 10 ‘Reduced inequalities’.
The proposed project idea focuses on two central themes: (1) enhancing the specific capacity and competence of project participants at the individual level
(2) increasing the partners’ organisational resilience and societal impact by expanding both the diversity of the skill sets they offer, as well as the profile of the project beneficiaries.
